messages:
dani: Heads up — ACME asking for a committed GPU pool quote. They want committed throughput that covers normal peaks but retain burst on top. Pricing sync Tue, need a sizing recommendation by EOD.

cj: Do we have their observed workload shape? spikes vs sustained? that will change commit vs burst tradeoffs.

dani: sent telemetry link: https://redwood.internal/telemetry/acme — TL;DR from last 30 days: 1h peak ~6.2k requests, median ~1.9k, 95th token/sec ~18k. typical request size ~1.5k tokens.

infra-bot: snapshot 2026-03-10T14:02Z — 30d window — peak_rps=6200; median_rps=1900; avg_tokens_per_req=1500; peak_tokens_per_sec=18000; current model variant=redwood/open-8k-v1

sahil: quick back-of-envelope: measured throughput for open-8k-v1 on H100-80 with our q4f16 path ~9k tokens/s per GPU at median batch sizes. so math below.

sahil: ```
peak_tokens = 18000
per_gpu = 9000  # measured tokens/sec per H100 for this model+quant
base_gpus = ceil(peak_tokens / per_gpu)  # => 2
committed = base_gpus + 1  # +1 cushion for queuing/maintenance => 3
burst_target = 6  # allow autoscale to double for short windows
``` 

cj: I agree with the cushion. Also factor in node failure/maintenance windows — we should size commit to cover p95 without relying on single-node redundancy. +1 GPU cushion seems right for their SLA.

kevin: For pricing: committing 3 GPUs in NA-west at current cloud rates gets us ~35% discount vs pure on-demand. But if they need burst to 6 occasionally we either: 1) autoscale to on-demand (higher unit cost) or 2) include prepaid burst credits in contract. Need to quantify expected burst minutes.

dani: ACME says bursts are usually 2–6 minutes and happen ~5x/day during business hours.

cj: rough cost model: commit 3 GPUs -> covers 95% of traffic. Burst 3 extra GPUs for up to 10 minutes/day -> small incremental cost. Operational note: set routing to prefer committed pool within region, fallback to burst pool in same region before cross-region.

sahil: ops config snippet (suggested):
```yaml
routing:
  - rule: prefer_committed
    pool: acme-dedicated-commit
    min_capacity: 3
  - rule: burst_fallback
    pool: acme-burst-on-demand
    max_burst: 6
    scale_policy: short-window (5m)
``` 

kevin: I'll model monthly spend vs on-demand and include a clause for burst overage billing. also check discount tiers if they commit 12+ months.

dani: OK team — please add final numbers in the pricing doc (sheet link) and I'll take to sales call. If anyone sees an outlier in telemetry that contradicts the per_gpu estimate speak now.

cj: quick sanity: I'll run a focused perf test tomorrow on H100-80 with their prompt set to validate the 9k tokens/s figure and post results.

sahil: I'll prepare a canary rollout plan for the committed pool (10% traffic -> 50% -> 100%) and a rollback path if latency regresses.

kevin: noted — I'll draft the contract language for committed capacity + burst credit billing.

dani: thanks — this is enough to draft quote. :white_check_mark:
